export const storyCode = `
{
  ...
  docs: {
    page: () => (
      <CurriStorybookWrapper
      title="Creating Stories for your UI Component"
      description="A brief description of creating stories."
      >
        <Heading size="h4" as="h2" fontWeight="medium">How to create a story</Heading>
        <Paragraph size="medium">
          This is how you create a story
        </Paragraph>
        <StorybookComponent />
      </CurriStorybookWrapper>
  }
}
`

export const defaultConfigCode = `
export default {
  /*
    argTypes: Configurable component props that can be toggled within the Sandbox tab.
    If you do not provide these, it will automatically generate the argtypes based on what the component props.
  */
  argTypes: {
    color: {
      // Defines the addon Controls to play with the props of the components. Look into https://storybook.js.org/docs/react/essentials/controls
      // for a list of possible controls
      control: {
        options: ['black', 'teal'],
        type: 'select',
      },
      defaultValue: 'black',
    },
    variant: {
      control: {
        options: ['filled', 'outlined'],
        type: 'select',
      },
      defaultValue: 'filled',
    },
  },
  /*
    component: Component you wish to render as a story
  */
  component: Button,
  /*
    decorators: Wraps a story in extra “rendering” functionality.Currently we have two decorators that we use, "withDesign" and "jsxDecorator".
    withDesign => ties a figma link to your Addons
    jsxDecorator => Displays the component JSX within the Addons
  */
  decorators: [withDesign, jsxDecorator],
  // Parameters are a set of static, named metadata about a story, typically used to control the behavior of Storybook features and addons.
  // If you want to disable an addon within parameters set the specific add on to disabled.
  // i.e. action: { disabled: true }, // disables and hides the action addon
  parameters: {
    https://storybook.js.org/docs/react/essentials/actions
    actions,
    /*
    Docs addon that we use to create documentation for a story.
    https://storybook.js.org/addons/@storybook/blocks
    */
    docs: {
      page: () => (
        ... // Look below for how we templatize the story documentation.
      )
    },
  }
  // Creates the title of the component as well as the side bar navigation of the story
  title: 'Component/Buttons/Default'
}
`

export const sampleStoryCode = `
{/* Primary Story */}
export const Button = (argTypes: ComponentProps<typeof ButtonComponent>) => {
  const { color, variant } = argTypes
  return (
  <ButtonComponent
    color={color}
    variant={variant}
  >
    {children}
  </ButtonComponent>
  )
}
{/* Second Story */}
export const BlackFilled = ({
  children,
}: ComponentProps<typeof ButtonComponent>) => (
  <ButtonComponent color="black" variant="filled">
    {children}
  </ButtonComponent>
)
`

<Meta
  title="About/Creating Stories"
  parameters={{
  previewTabs: {
      canvas: {
        hidden: true,
      },
    },
  viewMode: 'docs' }}
/>

<CurriStorybookWrapper title="Creating Stories" description="Documentation of how to setup a story for Curri UI Components.">
  <Heading size="h4" as="h2" fontWeight="medium">Creating Storybook Documentation</Heading>

  <Spacer value={15} />

  <Paragraph size="medium">
    Stories within Storybook provide documentation of a Curri UI component is built and used. There are two main ways of how this documentation
    is displayed, <code>Docs</code> and <code>Sandbox</code>. <code>Docs</code> are the documentation of the component whereas the <code>Sandbox</code>
    is an environment where you can test out editing the components.
  </Paragraph>

  <Spacer value={15} />

  <Paragraph size="medium">
    If this is your first time writing a storybook, feel free to look over at the storybook documentation of how
    to <a href="https://storybook.js.org/docs/react/writing-stories/introduction">write a story</a>. Described below is a way we
    create a new storybook file. Add the story file (<code>Component.stories.tsx</code>) within stories in their respective place where you think
    they should be organized in.
  </Paragraph>

  <Spacer value={5} />

  <Source language="jsx" dark format={true} code={defaultConfigCode} />

  <Heading size="h3" as="h2" fontWeight="medium">Docs Template</Heading>

  <Spacer value={15} />

  <Paragraph size="medium">
    We developed a template for you to write your storybook documentation. In the default configuration
    within <code>paramters.docs.page</code>, this is where the documentation will be written. These documentations will
    be displayed within the <code>Docs</code> tab. When building out the documentation, wrap your content within the <code>CurriStorybookWrapper</code>
    component. You would then build out your documentation similar to how you would build out any <code>JSX</code> file. Feel free to use
    the available components already provided such as <code>Heading</code>, <code>Paragraph</code>, <code>Grid</code> etc.
  </Paragraph>

  <Spacer value={15} />

  <Heading size="h5" as="h3" fontWeight="medium">Parameter definition</Heading>

  <Source
    language="jsx"
    dark
    format={true}
    code={`
docs: {
  page: () => (
    ... // Build out documentation here
  )
},
`
    }
  />

  <Heading size="h5" as="h3" fontWeight="medium">CurriStorybookWrapper Example</Heading>

  <Spacer value={15} />

  <Paragraph size="medium">
    Note: <code>CurriStorybookWrapper</code> has two props <code>title</code> and <code>description</code>. <code>title</code> creates
    the Header Title and <code>description</code> (optional), adds a subheader under the title.
  </Paragraph>

  <Source language="jsx" dark format={true} code={storyCode} />

  <Spacer value={5} />

  <Heading size="h3" as="h2" fontWeight="medium">Creating a Story</Heading>

  <Spacer value={15} />

  <Paragraph size="medium">
    Creating a named export Functional Component will create Story automatically within the storybook navigation. The props
    that are added <code>ArgTypes</code> are the props defined in the default export that are able to be passed down to the actual
    UI component. Creating additional exported named functional components will create more stories for your component. Example provided below.
  </Paragraph>

  <Source language="jsx" dark format={true} code={sampleStoryCode} />

  <Paragraph size="medium">
    For reference, feel free to look at <code>Button.stories.tsx</code> for an example of how a full story is written.
  </Paragraph>
</CurriStorybookWrapper>
